title: quanda: An Interpretability Toolkit for Training Data Attribution Evaluation
claim: Evaluating attribution methods is a standardized pipeline from prediction through attribution scores to multi-metric rankings, exposing each method's strengths and weaknesses.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, curved arrows labeling stages, bar charts at right
description: A wide three-stage diagram read left to right. The left panel shows a test image of a panda feeding into a small neural network that outputs the label "panda", with a training-data database and folder icons below it. Curved arrows labeled "Training Data Attribution" lead to the middle panel, a grid of four color-coded rows (orange, green, red, purple) of training image thumbnails. Each thumbnail carries an attribution score, ordered from low to high influence, with an ellipsis in the middle. A second curved arrow labeled "quanda" leads to the right panel, "Evaluation". There, grouped bar charts show each method's rank across five metrics: Class Detection, Mixed Dataset Separation, Top-K Cardinality, LDS and Mislabeling Detection. An arrow points to an Average Rank bar chart. A legend at the bottom names ReprPoints, TracInCP, EK-FAC and TRAK-1 by color. The eye goes first to the colorful image grid and the bars.
caption: Overview of exemplary benchmarking results facilitated by \quanda, instantiated on the AwA2/ResNet-50 setting. The figure depicts the training data attribution (TDA) evaluation pipeline: each TDA method generates attribution scores for test samples, and \quanda computes metric scores, assessing various aspects of attribution quality across different evaluation strategies. Each metric provides insight into a specific dimension of the attributor's performance, resulting in a comprehensive analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of each method. The full quantitative results for this setting are reported in [ref], and the experimental details are given in [ref].
abstract: Training data attribution (TDA) methods estimate the influence of individual training samples on a model's predictions, offering a principled lens for interpreting neural networks. Despite rapid methodological progress, TDA evaluation remains scattered across papers and rarely reproducible, making fair comparison between methods challenging. We introduce quanda, a Python toolkit that standardizes TDA evaluation. quanda features a comprehensive collection of evaluation metrics and ready-to-use benchmarks spanning image classification, text classification, and language modeling, alongside a uniform interface for integrating diverse TDA implementations. We showcase quanda through a comparative study of existing TDA methods and find that no approach excels uniformly across metrics, with clear trade-offs between ground-truth faithfulness and downstream task performance. By consolidating the tooling around TDA, quanda equips the community to evaluate attribution methods rigorously and reproducibly. The toolkit is thoroughly tested, documented, and available as an open-source library on PyPI and at https://github.com/dilyabareeva/quanda.
